reviews.rationale: Sequential comparison of selected GAAP quarterly rows shows higher net interest income and higher non-interest income, partly offset by a larger credit-loss provision and higher non-interest expense, leaving pretax and common-attributable net income modestly higher on a GAAP basis. Credit-quality signals are mixed rather than uniformly adverse: the annualized net charge-off rate is unchanged and the combined nonperforming-asset ratio is slightly lower, while nonaccrual loans rose and repossessed assets fell, and criticized/classified balances and special mention declined. The larger allowance stocks are consistent with a higher provision but the selected rows do not establish whether the driver was portfolio growth, migration, or specific credits. Non-interest income includes a Q3-only mortgage origination-and-sale gain line whose scope is not confirmed comparable to the Q2 line, so the non-interest income comparison cannot be attributed to a like-for-like business trend. All figures are sequential displayed-value arithmetic on selected rows, not year-over-year, not non-GAAP, and not guidance; no causal driver is asserted. Missing evidence includes full income statements and balance-sheet growth, net interest margin and average balances, allowance coverage relative to loan growth, charge-off composition, segment detail, non-GAAP reconciliations, and any forward guidance. Research state maintained at existing conviction with no trade; the view would change on evidence of sustained nonaccrual and past-due migration outpacing allowance build, or on confirmation that the non-interest income increase is not comparable in scope.
